title: Quggalune
summary: Quggalune is recorded as a locality in western Southampton, in the Quoquanantuck or Quogue purchase landscape near Assop's Neck.
history_content: The name appears in a 1738 town-record description for laying out the north division of the Quogue purchase. The town description connects the place with a highway, a creek crossing, and the head of a swamp.
translation_content:
The derivation is uncertain. The surviving record preserves Quggalune as a locality name rather than giving a clear translation.

Why Place Names Matter

“A place’s name is a juncture where language, culture and human thoughts or impressions meet.”

— Eko Nursanty, Investigating the Significance of Toponym to the Outstanding Local Values of Heritage Places for the City's Cultural and Economic Competitiveness (2021), Survey research paper, opening discussion
preservation_content: Quggalune preserves a small named place within the Quogue purchase, showing how roads, necks, creek crossings, and swamp edges were organized through Indigenous place-names in town records.
